Anya Patel: Heads up — during sable-30k-int4 bring-up I'm seeing context drift / token misalignment after ~22k tokens. Happens when prefetch=kv is enabled and RoPE scaling uses a cosine schedule. Repro below, can someone triage?

Anya Patel: Repro steps: `./run_infer --model sable-30k-int4 --quant=int4 --prefetch=kv --rope-schedule=cosine --ctx=32768 --prompt-file=tests/long_anchor.txt`

Anya Patel: Quick log excerpt (trimmed):
```
[22:01:12] kv_prefetch: window=65536 horizon=4096 prefetch_rate=0.25
[22:01:12] step=22000 pos=22001 rope_scale=0.998723
[22:01:12] kv_idx_write=4095 kv_idx_read=4096  <-- expected read==write-1 but see shift
```

Anya Patel: Output mismatch snippet (gold vs run):
```
... gold: "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog."
... run : "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy" + "dog ."  <-- extra space + token split
```

Devon: Can you paste the exact command and job id? I want to run the same harness with KV dump. Also try `--no-prefetch` to see if it goes away. :eyes:

Anya Patel: job id 1780000420. I'll try `--no-prefetch` now and post results.

ops-bot: Job 1780000420 queued on node gpu-a13; test-run metadata: trace=https://telemetry.internal/trace/1780000420 (expires in 7d)

Cara: I ran a quick smoke with the same model + linear-rope schedule (instead of cosine) and prefetch=kv enabled. No drift observed up to 28k tokens in my quick pass. So probably tied to schedule interactions. Job id 1780001112, trace=https://telemetry.internal/trace/1780001112

Mohammed: My hypothesis: the cosine schedule introduces fractional per-pos scaling factors that, when combined with int4 quant rounding, causes small per-position index offsets after the prefetch window boundary. Those accumulate and manifest as a 1-token read/write skew at certain boundaries (~multiples of 4096).

Mohammed: Quick experiment idea: force `rope_scale = round(scale * 2**N) / 2**N` (quantize scale to fixed-point) or use linear schedule and see if drift goes away. Also test `kv_prefetch_horizon=2048` to reduce exposure.

Eli: For reproability: set `KV_DUMP=1` + `KV_DUMP_DIR=/tmp/kv-dumps` and run single-shard (shard=0) with `--deterministic` flag. That will produce `kv_index_*` files so we can diff positions where read != expected.

Devon: Small parity-check Python snippet to spot index drift quickly:
```
def check_parity(positions, scale_fn, window):
    for pos in positions:
        scaled = scale_fn(pos)
        k_idx = int(round(pos * scaled)) % window
        # compare with dumped_kv[pos]
```

Anya Patel: Ran `--no-prefetch` — drift disappears. Ran `--rope-schedule=linear` with prefetch and drift also disappears. Attached KV dump diff of first mismatch at pos=22001 (trace 1780000420). Link: https://telemetry.internal/dumps/1780000420/diff.txt

Anya Patel: Sample problematic token contexts around 22000: before mismatch tokens look fine, after mismatch tokens split subword boundaries and punctuation shifts. Seems deterministic.

Mohammed: Sounds like accumulation + rounding. My immediate mitigation: clamp accumulated fractional offset each prefetch window boundary and snap to nearest integer index before performing the prefetch read. Also add an assert in dev build to verify `read_idx == (write_idx - 1) % window` at boundaries so we catch regressions.

Cara: I'll add a fuzzbench case for the onboarding checklist that runs cosine vs linear schedules under int4 quant with varying prefetch horizons (1024/2048/4096) and flags it if any token-level diffs appear vs reference. I'll run it tomorrow and send results.

Devon: Could also try alternative rounding rule: round-to-even vs floor. If quantization bias is directional that could explain consistent skew. Mohammed, wanna try patching rounding in the runtime and see CI fuzz results?

Mohammed: I'll prototype a rounding-to-even patch and run the local reproducer. ETA ~4h. If that helps, we can make it a runtime flag behind `--rope-rounding=even|floor|ceil` and default safe option for queued builds.

Anya Patel: Thanks everyone. Prioritizing as P2 but because it affects onboarding for this model, would like a small perf/backcompat patch if possible. I'll keep the job traces and KV dumps linked above.

infra-bot: Noted. Can add a Canary rollout that disables cosine schedule for queued hosted deployments of sable-30k-int4 until we have a fix. Ping @platform-ops if you want an emergency revert.

Cara: I'll open a small PR with the fuzzbench scenario + test matrix and assign to Mohammed + Devon for follow-up.

Anya Patel: Ack. Posting results in ~6h or earlier. :thumbsup:
